_readme: One sponsor slot per corridor page and per state/city camera page, directly above the live map.
Keys, tried most specific first. Corridor pages: corridor:<slug> → corridors:* → *. Camera pages: cameras:<state-or-city-slug> → state:<XX> → cameras:* → *.
So 'state:WA' covers the Washington page and every Washington city page (Seattle) but no corridor page, because corridors cross states. Buy a corridor with corridor:i-90.

Dates are inclusive YYYY-MM-DD in UTC. A slot outside its dates is skipped, and the next key is tried; with nothing left the house slot renders. Pages are static, so a date change takes effect when the pages are regenerated.

Fields: id (letters, digits, dashes; this is what the report groups by), name, copy (one sentence, under 90 characters), url (the sponsor's landing page, with their UTM if they want one), cta (2-4 words), logo (path under /images/sponsors/, PNG or SVG, transparent background, at least 2x for a 36px-tall display), logoW and logoH (the file's pixel size, so the browser reserves the box), start, end.

After any change, from the site root: node scripts/gen-corridor-pages.js && node scripts/gen-state-camera-pages.js && node scripts/gen-city-camera-pages.js && node scripts/tag-store-links.mjs --pt 128447811 && node scripts/add-analytics.mjs G-CDMSB5630W, then commit and push.
Counting and the report: docs/website-sponsor-slot.md in the app repo.

house.copy: One sponsor per page, on the website only. The app has no ads.

corridor:i-75.name: Example Tire
corridor:i-75.copy: Winter tires installed while you wait, 40 stores along I-75.
